feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: Gloria Steinem, trailblazing journalist and activist, dies at 92
entry.summary: At a time when women were largely limited to domestic roles, Steinem challenged gender stereotypes and championed feminist ideals like equality, sisterhood and reproductive freedom.

entry.title: As millions of kids lose SNAP food benefits, free school meals are also at risk
entry.summary: Food stamps have a direct link to other critical resources, such as free breakfast and lunch at school. Now, experts say they're starting to see that link break.

entry.title: Trump administration mulls renaming USS Doris Miller
entry.summary: The Trump administration is considering stripping the name of an African American war hero from an aircraft carrier, even though President Trump himself praised the honor in his first term.

entry.title: Jury is deadlocked in Lindsay Clancy's trial
entry.summary: Jurors in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman charged with murdering her three children, are deadlocked after five days of deliberation.

entry.title: Former top military leader on dismissals in the Pentagon under Secretary Hegseth
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with retired 4-star General Peter Chiarelli {ker-ELL-ee} about Pentagon leadership and the departure of top officials.

entry.title: Ex-military officials raise alarm over leadership departures from the Pentagon
entry.summary: Former U.S. military officials are raising alarms about the exodus of experienced leaders from the Pentagon, against the backdrop of the conflict with Iran and concerns over depleted stockpiles.

entry.title: New immigration court tactic leads to huge lines and chaos in Miami
entry.summary: Chaos unfolds at the Miami immigration court after judges are assigned mega master calendars, hearings where judges see more than 100 immigrants at once.

entry.title: Understanding the tech giants' oversized influence in American schools
entry.summary: Big tech companies like Apple and Microsoft use devices, training and conferences for teachers and students to embed in schools. The New York Times' Natasha Singer discusses the impact in Coding Kids.

entry.title: New lawsuits claim OpenAI execs put image ahead of safety in Canadian mass shooting
entry.summary: The suits say that recommendations to alert police about the alleged shooter were nixed by OpenAI's global affairs team, led by veteran political strategist Chris Lehane. OpenAI denies the claims.

entry.title: ICE detainee dies just hours after he was admitted into detention
entry.summary: Lianyong Wei's death marks the 57th death of an immigrant detainee held in the care of the government since the start of President Trump's second term. Twenty-four of those have occurred since Jan. 1.
